text: Choose ONE visual mode (Swiss Industrial Print or Tactical Telemetry) per project and commit to it. Do not alternate or mix both modes within the same interface.
If Swiss Industrial Print (Light): Set background to `#F4F4F0` or `#EAE8E3` (matte, unbleached documentation paper).
If Swiss Industrial Print (Light): Set foreground to `#050505` to `#111111` (carbon ink).
If Swiss Industrial Print (Light): Use `#E61919` or `#FF2A2A` (aviation/hazard red) as the only accent color for strike-throughs, thick structural dividing lines, or vital data highlights.
If Tactical Telemetry (Dark): Set background to `#0A0A0A` or `#121212` (deactivated CRT, avoid pure `#000000`).
If Tactical Telemetry (Dark): Set foreground to `#EAEAEA` (white phosphor) as the primary text color.
If Tactical Telemetry (Dark): Use `#E61919` or `#FF2A2A` (aviation/hazard red) as the accent color with same rules as light substrate.
If Tactical Telemetry (Dark): Optionally use `#4AF626` (terminal green) for exactly one status indicator or data readout, never as general text color.
Use heavy sans-serif web fonts (Neue Haas Grotesk Black, Inter Extra Bold/Black, Archivo Black, Roboto Flex Heavy, Monument Extended) for macro-typography.
Set macro-typography scale using `clamp(4rem, 10vw, 15rem)` for fluid viewport scaling.
Set macro-typography letter-spacing (tracking) to extremely tight values (`-0.03em` to `-0.06em`) to form solid architectural blocks.
Set macro-typography line-height (leading) to highly compressed values (`0.85` to `0.95`).
Use exclusively uppercase casing for macro-typography structural impact.
Use monospace web fonts (JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Space Mono, VT323, Courier Prime) for micro-typography (data and telemetry).
Set micro-typography scale to fixed small values (`10px` to `14px` / `0.7rem` to `0.875rem`).
Set micro-typography letter-spacing (tracking) to generous values (`0.05em` to `0.1em`) to simulate mechanical typewriter spacing.
Set micro-typography line-height (leading) to standard to tight values (`1.2` to `1.4`).
Use exclusively uppercase casing for all micro-typography metadata, navigation, unit IDs, and coordinates.
Reject `border-radius`. Use exactly 90-degree corners to enforce mechanical rigidity.
Utilize `display: grid; gap: 1px;` with contrasting parent/child background colors to generate razor-thin dividing lines.
Construct the DOM using precise semantic tags (`<data>`, `<samp>`, `<kbd>`, `<output>`, `<dl>`) to reflect the technical nature of the telemetry.
Implement CSS `clamp()` functions exclusively for macro-typography to ensure aggressive scaling while maintaining structural integrity across viewports.
Use ASCII characters to frame data points, e.g., `[ DELIVERY SYSTEMS ]`, `< RE-IND >`.
Use directional ASCII symbols `>>>`, `///`, `\\` as directional indicators.
Integrate registration (`®`), copyright (`©`), and trademark (`™`) symbols as structural geometric elements.
Integrate crosshairs (`+`) at grid intersections, repeating vertical lines (barcodes), thick horizontal warning stripes, and randomized string data (e.g., `REV 2.6`, `UNIT / D-01`).
Apply halftone and 1-bit dithering to transform continuous-tone images or large serif typography into dot-matrix patterns.
Apply CRT scanlines via `repeating-linear-gradient` to the background to simulate horizontal electron beam sweeps.
Apply a global, low-opacity SVG static/noise filter to the DOM root to introduce unified physical grain.
